news.title: 1st Test, day five: Conway and Ravindra fall, New Zealand 157/4 at lunch, still 195 behind; India close on victory
news.note: Result due today (NZ time). The Replay Room long is the priority: capture Cricinfo + Cricbuzz as soon as the match ends.

news.title: AP: India strikes twice before lunch, closes on victory over New Zealand in 1st Test
news.note: Second source for the day-five lunch score.

news.title: AFP/Dawn: India declare on a record 720/9 - the highest Test total ever made in New Zealand (past NZ's 715/6d v Bangladesh, Hamilton 2019) and India's highest overseas; lead 352
news.note: Headline number for a news Short and the replay. AFP also claims all top five scoring 80-plus is a first in Tests; verify against Cricinfo records before use.

news.title: Outlook day-four report: 720/9d is the highest Test total in New Zealand; Pant 128 off 153, Jurel 78 off 79; NZ 119/2 at stumps (Conway 59*, Ravindra 27*)
news.note: Second source for the record total. Pant: first Asian keeper with Test hundreds in all four SENA countries (claim, verify).

news.title: Cricket Times: claims all seven of India's first partnerships reached 50, a Test first; Pant's Test sixes at 108
news.note: Single source and it misreports Pant's sixes in the innings (13 vs AFP's 6): treat as a lead only.

news.title: Day-five live: Washington Sundar makes the first breakthrough of the day
news.note: Spin on day five at the Basin: a beat for the replay and the Christchurch preview.

news.title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, 15, becomes the youngest captain in men's T20 history, leading Bihar in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy
news.note: New angle on the RR-retained teenager: Rising Star Short.

ideas.why: The common line is that huge totals kill Tests. Count every 700-plus innings and how often the side won, drew or lost; Wellington adds a fresh data point.

ideas.title: The Lab: What 350-Run First-Innings Leads Do to the Fourth Day and Fifth Day
ideas.why: India led by 352 but batted second, so no follow-on and limited time. Model how often big leads earned late in a Test convert to wins, by overs left.
ideas.timing: Any time this week; evergreen with the Wellington hook.
ideas.data: Cricsheet men's Tests (filter info.gender == male; 2002 onward, labelled 'in our archive') for overs-remaining curves; headline figures cross-checked with Cricinfo.

ideas.title: What If India Had Declared at Lunch on Day Four (629/6)? | What If
ideas.why: India batted on from 629/6 to 720/9. Did the extra ninety-odd runs cost overs that decide the result? Use the actual run rate and NZ's survival rate.

ideas.title: Why Couldn't India Enforce the Follow-On With a 352 Lead? | Did You Know
ideas.why: The follow-on only applies to the side batting first. A 352-run lead with no follow-on option is a perfect explainer: Law, drawn example, the twist.
